A study sheet of separate single brush marks in black sumi ink on plain flat white paper, to be cut out as effect elements for a 2D game. Every mark stands alone with generous empty white space around it; no mark touches another or the edge of the sheet. Row one: three long horizontal strokes of a wide, half-dry brush, each starting with a pressed rounded head and ending in a tail of dry-brush streaks with flecks of white paper, in three ink tones: pale grey, medium grey, black. Row two: four short, slightly wavy horizontal ripple strokes in pale and medium grey, as used to suggest small waves on water. Row three: three soft, rising, curling wisps of very pale grey wash with feathered edges, like thin smoke from a chimney, each about as tall as a stroke in row one is long. Row four: three small flying seabirds, each made of only two or three curved black strokes for the wings (wings raised, wings level, wings lowered), and two round dots of black ink of different size.

Technique: real ink brushed by hand on absorbent paper: strokes swell and taper with the pressure of the brush, edges bleed slightly, dry-brush streaks are visible; ink only, no colour, no outlines around the marks, no shading. The paper is pure flat white without texture, fibres or shadows, evenly lit. Not a digital vector drawing, not a 3D render.

Traditional East Asian ink wash painting (sumi-e) on warm off-white rice paper: black ink ground on an inkstone and diluted into many grey tones, from the palest wash to rich black, applied with soft round brushes. Technique: few, confident brush strokes, each laid down once and never reworked; strokes swell and taper with the pressure of the brush and break into dry-brush streaks with flecks of white paper where the brush ran dry; wet strokes bleed a little into the absorbent paper with soft feathered edges; distant shapes in pale diluted ink, near shapes in dark concentrated ink; shapes are built from single washes without outline, next to a few calligraphic contour strokes. Large areas of the paper stay completely empty: the empty paper is the sky, the water and the mist, and objects dissolve into mist at their lower edges. Strong reduction: few objects, each suggested with a handful of strokes, no fine detail, no rendered textures, no hatching, no smooth shading. Black ink only; the single exception in the whole painting is the one red band of the lighthouse, a flat wash of vermilion. It must look like a real ink painting brushed by hand: not a photograph, not a 3D render, not a digital painting, not a pen or pencil drawing, not a woodblock print, not a postcard, no coloured sunset, no seal stamps, no calligraphy, no frame or border.
